fullPassage:
The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS (Global Positioning System) on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties, through techno- and bio-enhancement, will bring about ____________________.

* techno-utopian: 기술 낙관론자 ** amputation: 절라내기, 절단 *** post-literate: 탈문해화의

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology ①<u>involve</u> claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man ②<u>are</u> an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to ③<u>remember</u> things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are ④<u>becoming</u> post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 'every media extension of man'은 단수 주어이므로 is가 맞다. are(복수)는 수 일치 오류.
det.analysis:
✅ ② are → is: every + 단수명사 = 단수 취급
❌ ① involve — criticisms(복수) + 복수동사 → 적절
❌ ③ remember — 'have to + 동사원형' → 적절
❌ ④ becoming — 'are becoming' = 현재진행형 → 적절
det.tip: every + 단수명사 = 단수 동사. Every student is(○) / Every student are(✕)

questions.passage: Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, ①<u>who</u> cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed ②<u>that</u> every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things. It is thus possible ③<u>which</u> extensions of human faculties will bring about arrested development in the natural ④<u>evolution</u> of higher human faculties.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 'It is possible that ~' 가주어-진주어 구조에서 that이 와야 하는데, which가 쓰임.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ which → that: 'It is possible that ~' 구문. that절이 진주어
❌ ① who — 선행사 thinker(사람) → 적절
❌ ② that — 'claimed that ~' 접속사 → 적절
❌ ④ evolution — 명사 → 적절
det.tip: It is possible/likely/certain + that절. which는 관계대명사, that절 자리에 불가

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, ①<u>no one</u> can find their way about ②<u>without</u> it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens ③<u>filling</u> of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties will ④<u>bring about</u> arrested development.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 'screens full of pictures'(그림으로 가득한 화면). filling은 '채우는'이라는 뜻으로 문맥에 맞지 않고, 형용사 full이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ filling → full: 'screens full of pictures' = 그림으로 가득한 화면. full(형용사)이 screens를 후치 수식
❌ ① no one — 부정 대명사 → 적절
❌ ② without — 'find their way without it' → 적절
❌ ④ bring about — 'will bring about' = 초래하다 → 적절
det.tip: full of = ~로 가득한(형용사). filling = ~을 채우는(현재분사). 'screens full of ~'가 올바른 표현

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not ①<u>new</u>. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an ②<u>amputation</u>. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we ③<u>reject</u> screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human ④<u>faculties</u> will bring about arrested development.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서 화면에 의존(rely on)한다고 했는데, ③에서 reject(거부하다)로 바뀌어 있다. 탈문해화의 원인은 화면 의존.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ reject → rely on: 원문은 'rely on screens'. reject(거부)는 rely on(의존)의 반의어
❌ ① new — 원문 그대로
❌ ② amputation — 원문 그대로
❌ ④ faculties — 원문 그대로
det.tip: rely on(의존하다) ↔ reject(거부하다). 탈문해화 = 화면 의존의 결과

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization. McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who ①<u>cautioned</u> decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming ②<u>pre-literate</u> because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books. It is thus possible that extensions of human faculties, through techno- and ③<u>bio-enhancement</u>, will bring about ④<u>arrested</u> development in the natural evolution of higher human faculties.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문에서 post-literate(탈문해화)인데 ②에서 pre-literate(문자 이전의)로 바뀌어 있다. post = 이후, pre = 이전 — 의미가 완전히 다르다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② pre-literate → post-literate: post-(이후) ≠ pre-(이전). 탈문해화(문자 이후) = 화면 의존
❌ ① cautioned — 원문 그대로
❌ ③ bio-enhancement — 원문 그대로
❌ ④ arrested — 원문 그대로
det.tip: post- = 이후(post-war 전후, post-literate 탈문해화) / pre- = 이전(pre-war 전쟁 전, pre-literate 문자 이전)

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모든 미디어 확장은 절단(amputation) — 뒤의 예시(걷기 상실, 기억력 상실, 길찾기 상실)가 단서
det.analysis:
✅ ① amputation(절단): 예시가 모두 능력 상실을 보여줌
❌ ② innovation(혁신) — 긍정적. 능력 상실 예시와 모순
❌ ③ celebration(축하) — 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ liberation(해방) — 긍정적. 능력 상실 예시와 모순
det.tip: amputation = 절단. 차→걷기 절단, 하드→기억 절단, GPS→길찾기 절단

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: innovative solutions to humanity's oldest challenges
a harmonious balance between nature and technology
arrested development in the natural evolution of higher human faculties

det.korean: 기술 확장 → 능력 대체 → 고등 인간 능력의 자연적 진화 정지
det.analysis:
✅ ④ arrested development in the natural evolution of higher human faculties: 글 전체 논지의 필연적 결론
❌ ① innovative solutions — 긍정적. 비판적 논조와 모순
❌ ② harmonious balance — 조화가 아닌 능력 상실이 주제
❌ ③ medical breakthroughs — 의학과 무관
det.tip: 빈칸 추론: 글의 흐름 = 비판 → 절단 예시 → 탈문해화 → 결론(능력 퇴화)

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 기술 과잉 확장에 대한 비판은 최근에 새롭게 등장한 것이다.
McLuhan은 모든 미디어 확장이 절단이라고 주장했다.
기술 과잉 확장에 대한 비판은 인간 향상과 관련이 없다.

det.korean: 원문: 'every media extension of man is an amputation' → 모든 미디어 확장 = 절단
det.analysis:
✅ ② McLuhan의 핵심 주장 원문 일치
❌ ① 'not new'(새롭지 않음) → 불일치
❌ ③ 'Canadian'(캐나다인) → 미국이 아님
❌ ④ 'claims of dehumanization'(비인간화) → 관련 있음
det.tip: 내용일치: 국적(Canadian ≠ American), 시기(not new ≠ recently) 변조 주의

questions.passage: McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS (Global Positioning System) on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than print media, such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 개인 GPS가 생긴 후로 사람들은 그것 없이 길을 찾지 못한다.
컴퓨터 하드드라이브 덕분에 인간의 기억력이 더욱 강해졌다.
McLuhan의 철학에 따르면 우리는 점점 더 인쇄 매체에 의존하고 있다.
자동차의 등장으로 사람들은 더 많이 걷게 되었다.

det.korean: 원문: 'no one can find their way about without it' → GPS 없이 길 못 찾음
det.analysis:
✅ ① GPS 없이 길 못 찾음: 원문 일치
❌ ② '기억력 강해짐' — 'don't have to remember'(기억할 필요 없어짐) = 기억력 퇴화
❌ ③ '인쇄 매체 의존' — 'rely on screens rather than print media' = 화면 의존
❌ ④ '더 많이 걷게' — 'don't walk' = 안 걷게 됨
det.tip: 선지의 인과/방향을 반대로 바꾸는 것이 내용일치의 핵심 함정

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 기술 과잉 확장에 대한 비인간화 주장은 새로운 것이 아니다.
McLuhan은 기본적으로 기술 낙관론자이면서 비판적 사고가였다.
McLuhan에 따르면 미디어 확장은 인간 능력을 증대시키기만 한다.

det.korean: McLuhan은 미디어 확장이 절단(amputation)이라고 했지, '증대시키기만 한다'고 하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ '증대시키기만 한다' — 원문은 'amputation(절단)'. 확장이 곧 능력 상실이라는 역설
❌ ① 'not new' → 일치
❌ ② 'primarily a techno-utopian, but also a critical thinker' → 일치
❌ ④ 'rely on screens → post-literate' → 일치
det.tip: McLuhan의 역설: 미디어 extension(확장) = amputation(절단). 확장 = 증대가 아님!

questions.passage: The strongest criticisms of the overextension of technology involve claims of dehumanization, and these arguments are not new. Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: McLuhan의 기술 낙관주의가 현대 사회에 미친 긍정적 영향
기술의 과잉 확장이 인간 능력을 퇴화시킨다는 McLuhan의 경고
인쇄 매체와 디지털 매체의 장단점 비교
GPS와 컴퓨터가 일상생활을 편리하게 만든 사례

det.korean: 글의 핵심: 기술 과잉 확장 → 비인간화 → 미디어 확장 = 절단 → 능력 퇴화 경고
det.analysis:
✅ ② McLuhan의 경고: 기술 확장이 인간 능력 퇴화를 초래
❌ ① '긍정적 영향' — 글은 부정적 측면(amputation) 강조
❌ ③ '장단점 비교' — 비교가 아닌 일방적 비판
❌ ④ '편리' — 편리함이 아닌 능력 상실을 강조
det.tip: 주제: 반복 키워드(overextension, amputation, arrested development) + 부정적 논조

questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Technology: The Key to Human Progress
Why We Should Embrace Digital Media
When Extension Becomes Amputation: McLuhan's Warning

det.korean: '확장이 절단이 될 때: McLuhan의 경고' — 글의 핵심 역설을 담은 제목
det.analysis:
✅ ④ When Extension Becomes Amputation: 글의 핵심 역설(확장=절단)을 정확히 포착
❌ ① 'Key to Progress' — 글은 기술의 부작용을 경고
❌ ② 'Legacy in Communication' — 업적이 아닌 경고가 핵심
❌ ③ 'Embrace Digital Media' — 글은 디지털 의존을 비판
det.tip: 제목 = 주제의 함축적 표현. 역설(extension ↔ amputation)이 핵심

questions.passage: McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it. Based on McLuhan's philosophy, we are becoming post-literate because we rely on screens full of pictures, rather than <u>print media, such as books</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 print media, such as books가 이 글에서 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 디지털 화면을 보완하는 보조적 학습 도구
기술에 의해 대체되기 이전의 전통적 지적 활동 수단

det.korean: print media = 화면(screens) 이전의 전통적 지적 활동 수단. 기술 의존 이전에 인간이 직접 읽고 사고하던 매체.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 기술에 의해 대체되기 이전의 전통적 지적 활동 수단: 'rather than'으로 화면과 대비. 탈문해화 이전의 매체
❌ ① '구시대적 유물' — 부정적 뉘앙스가 너무 강함. 글은 print media를 긍정적으로 대비
❌ ② '보조적 도구' — 보조가 아닌 대체된 주된 매체
❌ ④ McLuhan은 print media를 적극 옹호하지 않음. 변화를 분석했을 뿐
det.tip: 함축의미: rather than 구조 → print media는 화면에 의해 대체된 것 → 전통적 지적 활동 수단

questions.passage: Canadian philosopher of the electronic age, Marshall McLuhan was primarily a techno-utopian, but he was also a critical thinker, who cautioned decades ago against too much human extension into technology. McLuhan famously claimed that every media extension of man is an amputation. For example, once we have a car, we don't walk to the shops any more; once we have a computer hard-drive, we don't have to remember things; and now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without <u>it</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것은?

det.korean: 'now that we have personal GPS on our cell phones, no one can find their way about without it' — it = personal GPS
det.analysis:
✅ ② personal GPS: 바로 앞에 언급된 'personal GPS'가 it의 지칭 대상. GPS 없이 길을 못 찾는다는 맥락
❌ ① hard-drive — 이전 예시의 대상
